庫賓琴是菲律賓及東南亞一帶的口弦類體鳴樂器，常見於馬京達瑙人及其他穆斯林與非穆斯: The kubing is a jew's harp idiophone of the Philippines and Southeast Asia, found among the Maguindanao and other Muslim and non-Muslim tribes and also in Indonesia. Its name has variants such as kobing and kolibau from one people to another, the bamboo ones mostly being called kubing and the sugar-palm-leaf ones karinta and so on. It is traditionally regarded as an intimate instrument, mostly used for close communication between family members or lovers; both men and women play it, women less often, and men also use it in short-range courtship.
庫賓琴為菲律賓竹製口弦琴，見於馬京達瑙族及其他菲律賓與印尼穆斯林、非穆斯林部落。: The kubing is a Philippine bamboo jew's harp, found among the Maguindanao and other Muslim and non-Muslim tribes of the Philippines and Indonesia. Its name differs from people to people: the Maranao call it kobing, the Tinguian kolibau, the Ibanag and Itawes kuribaw, the Kalinga ulibaw and the Toraja karombi. Besides bamboo, it is also made from sugar-palm leaf, called karinta among the Munano and ore-ore mbondu or ore Ngkale among the Buton.
庫賓琴音色清脆而獨特，具有明亮、穿透力強的質感，帶有輕微的金屬質地。其音域主要位: The kubing has a clear, distinctive timbre, bright and strongly carrying, with a faint metallic quality. Its range lies mainly in the upper middle register, and its tone is nimble and springy. Because it is built of bamboo, the instrument produces gentle overtones through the natural resonance of the bamboo itself, so the sound is warm rather than harsh. Compared with the full, heavy tone of the Western harmonica, the kubing is finer and more delicate, with the colour of tropical Southeast Asia. Its sound has both the crispness of percussion and the continuity of a wind instrument; every note is clearly distinct, producing a music that runs on like falling drops of water, full of expression and national character.
